Amit — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short worksheet (brightcart-pilot-MAP.xlsx) and a sample invoice PDF that walks through two weeks of traffic. High level:

- Token accounting: we meter at the per-request level but then apply grouping rules for context amortization when the same conversation prefix is reused within the billing window. That reduces duplicate charges for repeated prefixes.
- Prefix amortization: for this pilot we amortize 80% of a prefix after first full-charge if the KV cache shows reuse within a 24h window; remaining tokens are billed at a lower effective rate via a prefix credit.
- Micro-floor / rounding: we have a minimum charge floor applied per request type, not per-token. For on-demand short calls the floor is 30 tokens (charged as 30 even if 12 tokens used). For streaming/long-recall calls (>=8k context) we apply a micro-floor of 50 tokens only when the request would otherwise fall below that threshold and cannot be amortized by KV reuse. Exact text is in the invoice note.

Example (included in the workbook):
- Week sample: 4,200 short calls (median 120 tokens) + 46 long retrievals (avg 10,200 tokens).
- Naive per-token charge = X tokens * unit price -> $
- After prefix credits & amortization sample: invoice line reduces long-call net by ~18% and short-call effective billed tokens are ~2% higher due to the 30-token floor.

I flagged the detailed math in the workbook under the tab "TwoWeek_Sample_Calc". Let me know if procurement wants the numbers mapped to your chart of accounts — we can add an invoice-friendly breakdown.

Team — forwarding Amit's ask from BrightCart procurement. Procurement will want a concise, contract-friendly statement of the micro-floor and prefix amortization behavior and a sample invoice they can attach to the SOW. Can we agree on the following and I will send back as an amendment?

Proposed lines for SOW annex (draft):
1) Metering: Tokens are measured per API request and recorded to the customer's ledger.
2) Prefix amortization: For repeated usage of the same prompt prefix within a 24-hour window, Redwood will apply a one-time amortization credit equal to 80% of the prefix tokens for subsequent uses in the window. The prefix must be byte-identical and cached in the customer's KV cache to qualify.
3) Micro-floor: A minimum billing floor applies as follows: short call floor = 30 tokens per request; long-recall (>= 8k context) floor = 50 tokens per request. These floors are applied after amortization credits and before wholesale discounts.
4) Rounding: Token charges are rounded up to the nearest whole token for per-token metering and to the nearest billing increment (10 tokens) when aggregating invoice line items for readability.

Open questions I want your take on: a) are we comfortable saying "80%" or should that be variable (we used 80% in the pilot deck); b) do floors vary by SKU (pilot will use hosted API sku) or should they be tied to request latency class?

Notes: attachment brightcart-pilot-MAP.xlsx includes the sample invoice and the exact per-line math. I did a quick pass on the PDF draft of an invoice for procurement that uses the rounding rules above.

Kimberly / Karthik / Tessa — please reply with edits we can lock to send to Amit.

—Priyom

Priyom — thanks, that workbook is exactly what procurement needed. A couple of quick clarifications before we proceed: 

1) For prefix amortization, can you confirm whether the credit is applied at invoice generation or streaming time (i.e., do we see provisional charges in near-real-time and then a post-facto credit)? Procurement is worried about interim budget visibility.
2) For rounding: the business wants guaranteed deterministic rounding rules in the contract. Can you change the phrasing from "nearest billing increment (10 tokens)" to "round up to the next 10-token increment for invoice aggregation" so it's crystal clear?
3) Lastly, for the micro-floor — happy with the 30/50 split — but can you confirm that these floors are waived for pilot accounts billed under a committed capacity clause?

If you can confirm those three points in writing we'll attach your wording to the SOW and sign off.
